content.title: About
content.content: Soft pretzels are a baked snack made from yeasted dough, twisted into the classic knot shape and baked until lightly golden. They are sold ready‑to‑eat, without added salt and with a buttery coating that makes them tender and aromatic.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pretzels originated in Germany, where they were popular among monasteries.
The knot shape symbolizes crossed arms in prayer and historically allowed the bread to be hung on ropes for drying.
Soft pretzels are often served with a variety of dips: mustard, cheese sauce, chocolate.
In the United States, soft pretzels became a street‑food staple in the early 1900s, especially in Philadelphia.
Unsalted, buttered pretzels are suitable for people limiting sodium intake.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The dough provides complex carbs that give lasting satiety.

items.title: Contains vitamin B1
items.content: Thiamine, present in whole‑grain versions, supports the nervous system.

items.title: Small amount of iron
items.content: Iron contributes to hemoglobin formation and energy production.

items.title: Contains plant oils
items.content: The buttered surface adds beneficial fatty acids when a vegetable oil is used.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The soft texture makes chewing and digestion easier, especially for children and seniors.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Pretzels contain wheat, so they are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten intolerance.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rapid carbohydrate absorption can raise blood sugar levels.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: The buttery coating adds calories; those watching weight should control portions.

items.title: Sodium in butter
items.content: Although the product is unsalted, the butter may contain a small amount of sodium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels can be eaten straight from the package, sliced and served with dips, added to salads, or used as a base for sandwiches. They reheat well in a microwave or oven to restore softness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight bag in a cool, dry place. For longer storage, refrigerate to prevent drying out. Discard if mold or off‑odors appear.
